# AUTOSAR description of LionDriver

LionDriver described in AUTOSAR terms, so that an OEM or Tier-1 integrator can import it into a standard AUTOSAR
toolchain and see the software components, their ports and interfaces, the CAN frames and signals, and the checksum and
counter protection the system has today. It is the first part of what the project lead's industry calls a CSAR
(Configuration, Software and Architecture Repository, a Tier-1 toolchain term, not an AUTOSAR one).

**This is a description, not an AUTOSAR implementation and not a compliance claim.** Neither part of LionDriver is an
AUTOSAR stack: the panda safety firmware is bare-metal C on an STM32H7, and openpilot is a set of Linux processes on the
comma device's SoC. The file names their parts in AUTOSAR's vocabulary; it changes nothing they do, and it carries no
evidence credit.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| What | [`generated/liondriver-reference.arxml`](generated/liondriver-reference.arxml): AUTOSAR XML (ARXML) for the reference configuration CFG-001 (Toyota Corolla E210, TSS 2.0), with [`generated/summary.md`](generated/summary.md), a readable list of what it holds and where each part came from |
| Target | AUTOSAR Classic Platform R22-11, schema `AUTOSAR_00051.xsd`, chosen as a recent release that current toolchains import; a reversible choice (`RELEASE` and `SCHEMA` in the generator) |
| Status | Draft, AI-assisted (Claude), I0, not reviewed. Version 0.1.0 (the file's `SYSTEM-VERSION`) |
| Generated from | The [SysML model](../sysml/README.md), [WP-S-05](../../03-system/WP-S-05-hsi-specification.md) §4.2, §5 and §11 (through the model's `Signals.sysml`), the [trace data](../../trace/README.md), the [vehicle register](../../../docs/liondriver/vehicles/README.md) and, in opendbc at the pinned commit, the platform's DBC and the Toyota safety mode (`opendbc/safety/modes/toyota.h`, built as the reference build) |
| Tool classification | [WP-P-07](../../07-supporting/WP-P-07-tool-classification-qualification.md) TL-61, TCL1, no credit |
| Open question | Whether CI may validate against the AUTOSAR schema: [decision register](../../01-management/decisions/register.yaml) DQ-430 (§4) |

## 1. Where each element comes from

| AUTOSAR element | LionDriver element | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `COMPOSITION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE` `VehicleContext`, `LdSda`, `SocSoftware`, `SafetyMcuFirmware` | The vehicle context, the item LD-SDA, E-01 SoC software, E-03 safety MCU firmware | SysML `OperationalContext`, `LdSda`, `E-01`, `E-03` |
| `APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE` Proc_* | One per openpilot process the model names (pandad, card, controlsd, selfdrived, …). Each is a Linux process. E-02, the ML models, runs inside modeld and dm and is not a separate component | SysML children of `E-01` |
| `APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE` `SafetyLayer` | E-03a, the opendbc safety layer compiled into the panda firmware | SysML `E-03a` |
| `COMPLEX-DEVICE-DRIVER-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE` `PlatformFirmware` | E-03b, the panda board firmware. Described as a complex device driver because it owns the SPI, FDCAN, GPIO and audio hardware directly | SysML `E-03b` |
| `APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE` Ext_* | The vehicle ECUs at the item boundary: EPS, PCM, ABS/VSC, cluster, forward camera. Only their CAN interface to the item is described | SysML external elements; which frames each one exchanges is the generator's `PEERS` table, from those elements' descriptions and WP-S-05 §12.3 |
| Sender-receiver interfaces `If_Cereal_*` | The 23 cereal publisher-to-subscriber flows between the modelled processes | SysML `DataFlow` connections (WP-S-03 §9) |
| Client-server interface `If_PandaControl` | The 36 control requests of SPI endpoint 0, one operation each, with their gating and required treatment | WP-S-05 §4.2 |
| Sender-receiver interfaces `If_CanPacketsToMcu`, `If_CanPacketsToSoc` | The CAN packet stream over SPI endpoints 3 and 1 | WP-S-05 §4.3 |
| Client-server interface `If_SafetyHooks` | The RX, TX and forwarding hooks the firmware calls in the safety layer | `opendbc/safety/safety.h` |
| `CAN-CLUSTER` `VehicleCan_Bus0`, `CameraCan_Bus2` | The harness's vehicle side (panda bus 0) and camera side (bus 2), classical CAN at 500 kbit/s | WP-S-05 §3, §5 |
| `CAN-FRAME`, `I-SIGNAL-I-PDU`, `I-SIGNAL`, `SYSTEM-SIGNAL` | Every frame the item sends, receives, checks or forwards in the reference configuration, with all its DBC signals, scaling and layout | The DBC; the TX allow-list, RX checks and forwarding blocks of `toyota.h`; the frames WP-S-05 §11 names |
| Sender-receiver interfaces `If_<frame>` and the system's signal mappings | Each frame's signals as the data elements of the ports that send and receive it | As above |
| `I-PDU-TIMING` cyclic period, `I-SIGNAL-PORT` timeout | The nominal rate of the panda's RX check (or of its TX rate check for frames it sends), and the RX timeout of 5 periods | `toyota.h` |
| `END-TO-END-PROTECTION-SET` | The Toyota checksum and counter of each frame, and who checks them (§3) | The DBC's `CHECKSUM` and `COUNTER` signals; `toyota.h`; WP-S-05 §5, §12.3 |
| `GATEWAY` `Panda_CameraForwarding` | The camera frames the panda copies from bus 2 to bus 0 unchanged | `toyota.h` and `safety.h` (`safety_fwd_hook`); WP-S-05 §11.1 S-15 |
| `ECU-INSTANCE` `LD_SoC`, `LD_SafetyMcu`, `Ext_*` | E-04b's SoC, E-04a the safety MCU, and the vehicle ECUs | SysML `E-04a`, `E-04b` and the external elements |
| `SDG` `LionDriver.Source`, `.Trace`, `.HSI.*`, `.HwSignal.*` (special data in `ADMIN-DATA`) | The work product and SysML element each part comes from; the signals S-nn, TSRs, AOUs and integrity it carries; the 14 hardware/software responsibilities HSI-01…HSI-14 of view V-20, each with the AUTOSAR basic-software module that does the same job on an AUTOSAR ECU (an analogy, not a claim) | SysML `Signals.sysml` (WP-S-05 §11, §11.4), the trace data |

Every safety-relevant signal S-01…S-29 of WP-S-05 §11 and every responsibility HSI-01…HSI-14 is placed somewhere in the
file, and every TSR and AOU cited exists in the trace data; otherwise the generator fails. The WP-S-05 §5 RX table is
compared with `toyota.h`, and a difference also fails it.

## 2. What is not modelled

- **Behaviour and timing inside the components**: no internal behaviour, runnables, events, OS tasks or timing
  chains. The safety task, the watchdog and the FTTI budgets of WP-S-04 are not in the file.
- **The SoC–MCU link as a bus.** AUTOSAR's system template has no SPI bus. The link appears only as the interfaces
  between the two compositions; its transfer checksum and its missing counter are in the interface descriptions and
  WP-S-05 §4.
- **Hardware below where an RTE would be**: the relay, orientation sense, ignition, reset and boot pins, watchdog, siren
  and supply measurement are special data on `PlatformFirmware` (HSI-nn and S-22…S-29), not ports.
- **Hardware and harness** (E-04, E-05) as elements of their own: only as the two device ECUs and the two CAN buses.
- **Bus 1** (radar/OBD), the radar, the DSU frames, diagnostics, and the camera frames that are forwarded unchanged but
  carry no LionDriver signal: the gateway says every other camera frame is forwarded the same way.
- **Frames allowed but not used by the reference car**: the TX hook allows `0x1D2` (cancel) and `0x283` from the
  SoC, and `0x750`; the rate-check notes in `toyota.h` say the reference car sends none of them, so the item is not
  their sender here. `0x750` is not in the DBC. `generated/summary.md` lists them.
- **Other configurations**: SecOC, LTA, the alternative brake and stock longitudinal Toyota modes, and every other
  brand. The reader refuses them rather than describe them wrongly.
- **Value tables** (DBC `VAL_` enumerations) and units beyond the DBC's unit strings.

## 3. Communication protection: what the file does and does not claim

The reference car has no AUTOSAR E2E profile on any frame, and the file does not pretend otherwise. Each checksum is
written as an `END-TO-END-PROTECTION` with category `LIONDRIVER_TOYOTA_CHECKSUM8`, which no AUTOSAR tool knows: it is
the Toyota 8-bit additive checksum over identifier, length and data, with the counter where the DBC has one, and the
description says who checks it. In short (WP-S-05 §12.3):

- frames the item **sends** (`0x2E4`, `0x343`, `0x412`, `0x191`) are packed by openpilot on the SoC; the panda does not
  check their checksum or counter; the EPS is assumed to (WP-S-05 OI-9);
- frames the item **receives** carry at most a checksum and no counter; the panda checks the checksum where its RX check
  says so and the timeout on all of them;
- the camera's **PCS frames** are forwarded byte for byte and checked by the receiving ECU; the panda is a black channel
  for them.

For comparison, WP-S-05 §12.5 notes that Volkswagen MQB uses CRC-8H2F with a data ID per counter value, the AUTOSAR E2E
profile 2 pattern; a second configuration on such a car would be described with `PROFILE_02`. No such vehicle is
configured. **SecOC**: none on the reference car; every PDU says so in its special data (AOU-18).

## 4. How it is generated and checked

```sh
python3 tools/gen_arxml.py            # write generated/ (needs the opendbc submodule)
python3 tools/gen_arxml.py --check    # fail if generated/ is not what the sources give today
python3 tools/check_arxml.py          # structural check A1-A8
python3 tools/check_arxml.py --xsd PATH/AUTOSAR_00051.xsd   # also A0, schema validation (needs lxml)
python3 tools/test_arxml.py
```

CI runs the first, third and last in the job "autosar description" of `.github/workflows/assurance.yaml`: a change to
the model, WP-S-05, the trace data, the vehicle register or the opendbc pin that changes the description fails until it
is regenerated.

**Schema validation.** The AUTOSAR XML schema is published by AUTOSAR for "informational purposes only"; other use
needs its written permission, and its redistribution is restricted. It is therefore not committed and CI does not fetch
it. CI runs A1-A8 instead, a structural check written for this project
([`tools/check_arxml.py`](tools/check_arxml.py)): identifiers, unique names per parent, every reference resolving to an
element of the type it names, ports typed by interfaces, connectors joining matching ports, every component mapped to
one ECU, one sender per frame, and the statement of what the file is. It does not check element order or the
schema's value patterns. The file was validated once against `AUTOSAR_00051.xsd` (R22-11, downloaded from
autosar.org on 2026-10-30, used for information only): **valid**, A0 passes. Whether CI may download the schema and
validate every change is the lead's question DQ-430.
